2. Communication and collaboration

Communication and collaboration capability helps Queensland Government employees interact, share knowledge, work effectively with others, participate in digital environments, support inclusive communication and manage their digital presence and reputation.

Official DigComp 3.0 area description

To interact, share, communicate and collaborate in digital environments while being aware of cultural, generational and other diversity and the features and limitations of digital technologies. To participate in society through digital technologies. To assert one's rights and exercise choice in digital environments. To manage one’s digital presence, identity and reputation.

Why this area matters

Queensland Government work depends on communication, collaboration and engagement across teams, agencies, stakeholders and communities.

Employees regularly communicate using Teams, Outlook, SharePoint, online collaboration platforms and digital services. Strong capability in this area helps people communicate appropriately, collaborate efficiently, participate safely in digital environments and manage their digital identity professionally.

Using workplace tools

Tool availability and approval varies across agencies.

Employees should only use approved communication, collaboration and AI-enabled tools in accordance with agency requirements, information security obligations, privacy obligations and records management requirements.

2.1 Interacting through and with digital technologies 2.2 Sharing through digital technologies 2.3 Engaging in citizenship through digital technologies 2.4 Collaborating through digital technologies 2.5 Digital behaviour 2.6 Managing digital identity

2.1 Interacting through and with digital technologies

What it is

Using appropriate digital tools and channels to communicate, engage and interact with individuals, groups and technology in different contexts.

Why it matters in Queensland Government

Choosing the right communication channel improves efficiency, reduces misunderstandings and helps government staff communicate effectively with colleagues, stakeholders and customers.

Workplace scenarios

  • Choosing between Teams chat, email or a meeting
  • Participating in virtual workshops
  • Using Microsoft Teams channels appropriately
  • Engaging with Copilot and AI assistants responsibly
  • Communicating across agencies

Tools and processes

  • Microsoft Teams
  • Outlook
  • Copilot Chat
  • SharePoint comments
  • Yammer / Viva Engage where applicable
  • Video conferencing

Try it at work

Review a recent work communication and ask:

  • Was the right channel used?
  • Was the purpose clear?
  • Was action required?
  • Was the audience appropriate?
  • Could the communication have been more efficient?
Official DigComp 3.0 proficiency statements

Basic

Uses familiar digital communication tools and channels to interact with guidance in everyday situations.

Intermediate

Selects appropriate communication channels independently and adapts interactions to different audiences and contexts.

Advanced

Combines communication methods effectively for complex interactions, supports others and manages collaboration across systems.

Highly advanced

Designs communication approaches, leads complex digital interactions and governs inclusive participation across digital environments.

Suggested next practice: Experiment with different communication channels during the next project and reflect on which was most effective.

Relevant resources

  • Microsoft Learn – Microsoft Teams
    Guidance for using Teams effectively in workplace collaboration.
  • APS Academy – Collaboration and communication
    Australian Public Service learning for communication and teamwork skills.
  • QUT communication resources
    Practical communication guidance and tools for professional contexts.

2.2 Sharing through digital technologies

What it is

Sharing information, knowledge and content ethically, responsibly and securely using digital technologies.

Why it matters

Government employees frequently share information across teams and agencies. Knowing when and how to share information safely is critical.

Workplace scenarios

  • Sharing files in Teams
  • Managing SharePoint permissions
  • Sharing reports and presentations
  • Providing information to stakeholders
  • Sharing lessons learned

Tools and processes

  • Microsoft Teams
  • SharePoint
  • OneDrive
  • Outlook
  • Collaboration platforms

Try it at work

Review how one recently created document was shared and assess whether permissions, security and accessibility requirements were appropriate.

Official DigComp 3.0 proficiency statements

Basic

Shares simple content using familiar tools and follows basic sharing rules with support.

Intermediate

Chooses appropriate sharing settings, applies access controls and shares content responsibly across teams.

Advanced

Manages secure and effective sharing workflows, considers audience needs and integrates collaboration tools.

Highly advanced

Leads sharing strategies, ensures compliance with security and privacy requirements, and promotes trustworthy information exchange.

Suggested next practice: Use Queensland Government, APS Academy and Microsoft learning resources relevant to secure and effective information sharing.

2.3 Engaging in citizenship through digital technologies

What it is

Using digital technologies to participate in communities, government services, consultation activities and wider society.

Why it matters

Queensland Government employees often engage with citizens, communities, businesses and stakeholders using digital platforms.

Workplace scenarios

  • Participating in consultation activities
  • Using Queensland Government digital services
  • Accessing public participation channels
  • Supporting community engagement

Tools and processes

  • Queensland Government websites
  • Consultation platforms
  • Have Your Say Queensland
  • Public engagement platforms
Official DigComp 3.0 proficiency statements

Basic

Participates in straightforward digital community or service activities with guidance and familiar tools.

Intermediate

Engages in online civic and service platforms independently and contributes to community or stakeholder consultations.

Advanced

Supports broader digital participation, advises on engagement channels and encourages meaningful contribution.

Highly advanced

Leads digital citizenship practices, shapes participation strategies and evaluates engagement across diverse stakeholders.

Relevant resources

  • Queensland Government consultation resources
    Information on government consultation and public participation channels.
  • Australian Public Service resources
    APS guidance on digital engagement and public service professionalism.
  • DigComp reference materials
    Official DigComp documentation and practical framework references.

2.4 Collaborating through digital technologies

What it is

Using digital technologies to work together, co-author information, coordinate work and achieve shared outcomes.

Why it matters

Modern public sector work relies heavily on virtual collaboration across multiple locations, teams and agencies.

Workplace scenarios

  • Co-authoring documents
  • Managing a Teams workspace
  • Multi-agency project delivery
  • Workshop collaboration
  • Virtual project meetings

Tools and processes

  • Teams
  • SharePoint
  • OneNote
  • Miro
  • Planner
  • Loop
Official DigComp 3.0 proficiency statements

Basic

Works with others using familiar collaboration tools and contributes to shared tasks with support.

Intermediate

Coordinates collaborative work, co-authors content and maintains shared spaces effectively.

Advanced

Drives multi-party collaboration, integrates tools for complex teamwork and supports shared outcomes.

Highly advanced

Leads collaborative digital initiatives, guides effective teamwork practices, and improves collaboration across agencies.

Suggested next practice: Include practical learning resources for Teams, SharePoint and collaborative working.

2.5 Digital behaviour

What it is

Communicating and behaving respectfully, ethically and inclusively in digital environments.

Why it matters

Professional behaviour influences workplace culture, public trust and collaboration outcomes.

Workplace scenarios

  • Online meetings
  • Digital discussions
  • Written communications
  • Respectful stakeholder engagement
  • Working across diverse teams

Tools and processes

  • Teams
  • Outlook
  • Collaboration platforms
  • Digital communication standards
Official DigComp 3.0 proficiency statements

Basic

Follows basic digital conduct expectations and behaves respectfully in familiar digital spaces.

Intermediate

Communicates professionally and inclusively, adapting behaviour to digital contexts and audiences.

Advanced

Promotes ethical digital behaviour, supports inclusive communication and models respectful online conduct.

Highly advanced

Shapes digital conduct standards, leads professional behaviour initiatives and fosters trust in digital interactions.

Suggested next practice: Include links to Queensland Government standards and professional communication resources.

2.6 Managing digital identity

What it is

Managing digital identities, digital footprints and professional reputations in online environments.

Why it matters

Employees represent themselves, their teams and often Queensland Government online.

Workplace scenarios

  • Professional online profiles
  • Managing permissions
  • Account settings
  • Privacy settings
  • Online reputation management

Tools and processes

  • Microsoft account settings
  • Queensland Government systems
  • Privacy controls
  • Identity management tools
Official DigComp 3.0 proficiency statements

Basic

Maintains a basic professional digital identity and follows simple privacy practices with guidance.

Intermediate

Manages account settings independently, protects privacy and presents a professional online presence.

Advanced

Coordinates digital identity practices across services, monitors reputation and ensures consistent professional representation.

Highly advanced

Leads digital identity governance, balances privacy and visibility, and guides others in managing online reputations.

Relevant resources

  • Office of the Australian Information Commissioner
    Privacy guidance for managing online personal and professional information.
  • Queensland Government privacy resources
    Guidance on privacy obligations and identity management in Queensland Government systems.
  • APS Academy resources
    APS learning on professional online identity and trusted government communication.
